messages:
alex-cs: FYI customer bryce (acct: brightpay) opened a legal hold — they say objects with `preserve:true` are not present in their export. see sample ids: obj_8f3a, obj_c12b. urgent, legal wants timeline. :rotating_light:

bryce-customer: Confirming — exported archive shows those ids missing but UI still marks them preserved. Downloaded export at 2026-03-16T18:02Z. We need a preservation proof for litigation hold.

elaine-support: Sorry you're seeing this, bryce. Can you paste the exact export filename and the API call you used? Also does the account have any custom retention policies or was it default?

bryce-customer: export: brightpay-legal-2026-03-16.tar.gz. call was our internal script hitting /v1/exports/brightpay/download (auth token redacted). Policy looked default from UI — we didn't set custom TTL.

elaine-support: pinging infra + kms for timeline. jon — can you check tombstone propagation + whether tombstones were applied to these objects around 2026-03-15 22:00 UTC?

jon-engineer: looking. quick Q: do you have the retention_policy_id for the account or one of the object metadata blobs? run: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/objects/obj_8f3a | jq '.metadata.retention_policy_id, .metadata.preserve'`

bryce-customer: ran that, got: `"policy_default_v3"` and `true` for preserve.

jon-engineer: hmmm. preserve:true but missing from export could mean export job enumerated storage index before prefix propagation finished, or export pipeline filtered tombstoned objects. Need object storage tombstone timestamps and index export window. infra-pager: can you pull the index snapshot times for brightpay export window?

infra-pager: grabbing logs now. also bumping retention team. :eyes:

kms-bot: NOTE: key rotation event for customer brightpay at 2026-03-14T03:12:05Z. No KMS deny recorded for export job id export_998.

jon-engineer: that rotation shouldn't delete objects but could change decryptability for archived blobs if key metadata wasn't attached to the export worker. Can you confirm export worker had access to key version used for those blobs?

elaine-support: @sara-legal requested we pause any automatic purge and mark case RED until we verify. Sara, are we requesting an immediate retention freeze?

sara-legal: Please pause purge for brightpay account and preserve all retention-related logs + exports. We need a chain-of-custody for the objects in question. Also confirm whether export included tombstones vs storage objects.

infra-pager: Export job export_998 started at 2026-03-16T17:58:02Z, manifest generation window: 2026-03-16T17:50:00Z -> 2026-03-16T17:58:00Z. Index snapshot used: idx_snapshot_2026-03-16T17:49:58Z. Objects obj_8f3a and obj_c12b were tombstoned at 2026-03-15T22:01:10Z and 2026-03-15T22:01:12Z respectively — so they predate the snapshot.

jon-engineer: If tombstones predate snapshot, they should be included as preserved entries in the manifest. Two possibilities: (1) export worker filtered tombstones client-side (bug), (2) manifest contained entries but subsequent bucket read failed due to key metadata mismatch. Let's fetch the raw manifest and worker logs. Command for raw manifest: `curl -s https://internal.redwood/export-manifests/export_998/manifest.json`

elaine-support: Manifest pulled, attaching excerpt: ```[ {"object_id":"obj_8f3a","status":"tombstone","preserve":true},{"object_id":"obj_c12b","status":"tombstone","preserve":true} ]```

bryce-customer: that's what we expected to see. So why were they absent in the tarball?

jon-engineer: grabbing worker logs for export_998. snippet: ```2026-03-16T17:58:05Z worker: fetching object obj_8f3a -> s3://redwood-archives/brightpay/obj_8f3a.enc 2026-03-16T17:58:06Z worker: s3 GET 403 for obj_8f3a (KMS: key_version_not_found) 2026-03-16T17:58:06Z worker: skipping object obj_8f3a due to read error```

kms-bot: audit: key_version_not_found for key brightpay-main at 2026-03-14T03:12:05Z (rotation). Looks like object file encrypted with old key version which was not present on export worker's keyring.

jon-engineer: that explains missing blob content. But tombstone entries should still appear as placeholders in export — we need to check the tar bundling logic that excludes entries when object file read fails.

elaine-support: next steps: jon to file a bug for export worker bundling skipping preserved tombstones on read errors; infra to re-run export with key fallback for read-only access; kms to provide the key material or a wrapped key so worker can include placeholders; legal to confirm freeze until re-run. I'll coordinate with the customer.

jon-engineer: filing issue now: INF-EXPORT-4521 — summary: export worker drops preserved tombstone entries when S3 read returns 4xx. Adding repro steps and logs.

infra-pager: scheduling manual re-run of export_998 with key fallback at 2026-03-16T20:00Z. Will post results.

sara-legal: Confirmed hold. Please include timestamped evidence that objects were preserved at time of tombstone and preserved flag was set.

elaine-support: bryce, we will re-run and provide a signed manifest + worker logs and the re-generated tarball. Apologies for the disruption. Will follow up in this thread when done. :white_check_mark:

bryce-customer: thanks — appreciate the quick escalation.

jon-engineer: note for postmortem: consider a change to bundler to still include zero-byte placeholder files for preserved tombstones even if read fails, and add a KMS key-version fallback to export workers.

infra-pager: re-run complete — archived file now includes `preserved_manifest.json` and placeholder entries for obj_8f3a and obj_c12b. uploading artifact to secure share (link redacted).

elaine-support: artifact uploaded and shared to legal. closing loop with customer.

bryce-customer: received — manifest and logs look good. legal team satisfied for now. thank you. :pray:
